solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet Laureate and fit dog

blocks.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for Poet Laureate
an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A poet laureate composes verse about a dog having a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to pester and harass them persistently, which is exactly what plaguing them means as a verb.

clue.text: Fag end in papa’s coat

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, enclosed by its outer letters

blocks.note: Chambers gives lag as the hindmost or last part, the fag end
papa is P in the radio alphabet, and the letter P is spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: A cigarette stub has ended up in the pocket of Dad's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag end is British slang for a cigarette butt, but here it means the last part of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelage is the zoological term for the fur, hair or wool covering a mammal, its natural coat.

clue.text: Unordained though privileged parishioner set page right

blocks.note: to lay something is to set it down
the recto is the right-hand page of an open book
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A churchgoer without holy orders but with special status puts a page straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay rector is a layman entitled to a parish's great tithes, holding rectorial rights without being a clergyman.

clue.text: Want muscles? No charge in middle of week

indicators.note: middle of asks for only the central letters of the following word, dropping its ends
in places one piece within the letters of another

blocks.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
the two central letters of the word week
N/C is the abbreviation for no charge

explanation.surface: A gym-goer wonders whether to buy toned muscles midweek when there is no fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or deficiency matches absence, the state of something not being present.

clue.text: Previously plotted against subordinate with difficult time

blocks.note: someone subordinate is under another
W is an abbreviation for with
a rough time is a difficult one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone was schemed against by a junior colleague during a hard period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks an archaic word: to underwork once meant to undermine or plot against secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwrought is the old past participle of underwork, meaning secretly undermined, so it describes someone schemed against in former usage.

clue.text: Person who’s dependent on amino acid for old eye remedy

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: in marketing's social grades, E is a person with no regular income, dependent on state benefit
serine is one of the amino acids found in proteins

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on a protein building block is told to use an old remedy for their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: E as a social grade is in Chambers: the lowest grade in advertising's ABC1 scale, people relying on benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Eserine, also called physostigmine, is a Calabar bean alkaloid once widely used in drops to contract the pupil and treat glaucoma.

clue.text: Legal eagle is fair about sticker on Indonesian car

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: just means fair
RI is the international vehicle registration code shown on a sticker on Indonesian cars

explanation.surface: A lawyer judges fairly in a dispute over a sticker on a car from Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: International vehicle registration codes, shown on oval stickers, are a common source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal eagle is an informal term for a sharp lawyer, and a jurist is an expert in law.

clue.text: Judge unopened tinnie as sweet in Oz

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening, its first letter

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
in Australian slang a tinnie, a can of beer, is also called a tube

explanation.surface: An Australian judge treats a sealed can of beer as a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and New Zealand a jube is a chewy fruit gum, short for jujube, a common confection there.

clue.text: Who’d grab solution for redevelopment?

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters of both words are used

explanation.surface: A question about who would seize on an answer to a city's renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: a city planner is the person who looks for answers to urban renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbanologist studies towns and city life, so would be the specialist seeking a fix for regenerating urban areas.

clue.text: Carriage some aristocrat hailed

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

blocks.note: found across the two words, from the end of aristocrat into hailed

explanation.surface: A nobleman summoned a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is an Indian chariot or four-wheeled vehicle, often drawn by horses or oxen, so a kind of carriage.

clue.text: International clown enjoying success

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for international
a nit is a fool or clown

explanation.surface: A world-famous clown is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in it, as in 'in it to win it', describes being in contention and doing well in a competition.

clue.text: Very small shirt not specified by hostel

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
NS is the abbreviation for not specified
the Y is short for the YMCA or YWCA, a hostel

explanation.surface: A tiny shirt with no size given turns up at a youth hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: Teensy is an informal, childish word meaning tiny, used of something extremely little.

clue.text: What’s paid in case urn gets smashed?

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A cover premium paid in case a precious vase gets broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is the regular premium handed over to a company against loss, so it is something regularly paid out.

clue.text: As told gags cause breakdown

indicators.note: as told means as spoken, so the word is wanted by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a gag can mean a made-up story or hoax, so gags are fibs

explanation.surface: Jokes retold cause someone to collapse with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lyse is the biological verb for causing a cell to disintegrate by rupturing its membrane.

clue.text: Debit? Be prepared for what goes out

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An accountant warns that a debit means money going out of the account.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb tide is the receding tide, the water flowing back out to sea.

clue.text: No longer declare a wine European

blocks.note: taken as written
red is red wine
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone stops naming a wine as European.
explanation.definitionFit: Arede is an archaic Spenserian verb meaning to explain or tell, hence obsolete for declare.

clue.text: Cautious about leaving camp occupied

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that piece goes out of the word

blocks.note: to camp is to tent, live under canvas
C is short for circa, about
busy or occupied means active

explanation.surface: A wary soldier gets out of a camp that has been taken over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal; here it is circa, the piece that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means hesitant and uncertain, proceeding carefully without commitment, so it fits wary.

clue.text: Engineer scam about, eg, ibuprofen and paracetamol

indicators.note: about can mean round and around, so the letters are turned around into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A con man sets up a fraud involving common painkillers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like the anagram signal; it is fodder, and the signal is 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen and paracetamol are non-proprietary drug titles as opposed to brand names like Nurofen or Panadol.

clue.text: There in Rome wine expert is absent

indicators.note: is absent says one part is missing and must be taken away from the longer word

blocks.note: prosecco is an Italian sparkling wine
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: In Rome a wine connoisseur is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecco is the Italian word for here it is or there, used when pointing something out.

clue.text: Old difficulty back in marshal’s retention of youth?

indicators.note: back means read in the backward direction
in places those letters within the name that follows

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a net is a snare or entanglement, a difficulty
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A veteran marshal is struggling to keep his youthful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both Old and difficulty together, not just the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoteny is the persistence of juvenile features into adulthood in an animal, such as the axolotl, so keeping youthful traits.

clue.text: Sappers collectively lifted explosives — they single out nobility

indicators.note: lifted means raised up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: sappers are army engineers, collectively the RE, Royal Engineers
mines are buried explosives

explanation.surface: Army engineers raise explosives, and they pick out the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is reversed to ER and followed by MINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine fur trims the robes of peers, so ermines mark out members of the aristocracy at ceremonies.

clue.text: Type of lasting quality starts to emulate neat artist

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of emulate and neat
Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance artist

explanation.surface: A durable sort of person begins to copy a tidy painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An endurer is someone who holds out and survives hardship, a person with staying power or stamina.

clue.text: Series involving support and Republican governor

indicators.note: involving means including, so one word holds the others inside

blocks.note: SER is an abbreviation for series
a golf tee supports the ball
R is short for Republican

explanation.surface: A run of events involves backing a Republican state governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A steerer controls direction, and governor in its original sense is a helmsman or pilot who steers.

clue.text: Substantive covering stuff to soothe itch in some places

indicators.note: covering means lying round the outside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: SB is the abbreviation for substantive, a noun
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: Someone using a noun to cover cramming material for relief from an itch.
explanation.definitionFit: Scramb is a dialect verb meaning to scratch, which is what you do to relieve itching skin in certain regions.

clue.text: Keen on wearing stuff pulled from bins mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
Chambers has tot as anything salvaged from rubbish

explanation.surface: A scavenger is fond of wearing clothes rescued from dustbins.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is a colloquial way to say you are enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Headless blusterer who’s fond of mystery

indicators.note: headless means the word loses its head, its first letter

blocks.note: a royster is a rowdy, swaggering blusterer

explanation.surface: A beheaded braggart turns out to love a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives oyster as a close, uncommunicative person, someone who keeps secrets tight shut like a shellfish.

clue.text: Time for bacon and eggs in hot old colony with Pam

indicators.note: hot suggests something heated and agitated, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breakfast time with Pam in a sweltering former colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Collop Monday is the day before Shrove Tuesday, when collops of bacon with eggs were traditionally eaten.

clue.text: Rifles, many loaded with round

indicators.note: loaded with means filled with, so the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: lots means many
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Plenty of guns are each loaded with a single cartridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifles' and 'round' suggest firearms; rifles is the verb, to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and plunder it, which is what someone does when they loot it.

clue.text: Swinney’s worthless on account of admitting vacuous rancour

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of the word stay
admitting means letting in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: O/A is the abbreviation for on account of
the first and last letters of rancour

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician's remarks are dismissed as pointless bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: John Swinney is a Scottish politician, so the definition asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is a Scots adjective meaning odd or unattached, hence good-for-nothing or of no value.

clue.text: Turn up this large fish

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to slew is to turn or swing round

explanation.surface: An angler hauls up a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The wels is a huge European catfish, also called the sheatfish, which can grow to several metres long.

clue.text: Clogs left in narrow passages

indicators.note: in tells us to place one piece within the other

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
guts are narrow channels or straits

explanation.surface: Wooden shoes are abandoned in tight alleyways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clogs' suggests shoes; here it is a verb, to block up.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut something is to choke or overload it, so it clogs as a verb meaning to block.

clue.text: New car and one must accept end of Stirling Moss, say

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are made into a fresh order
end of means just the final letter of the word
to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of Stirling

explanation.surface: A new car for racing driver Stirling Moss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirling Moss' reads as the racing driver; Moss is the definition and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrogen is a flowerless plant growing at the tip, such as ferns and mosses, so a moss is one example.

clue.text: Backbone in lamb

blocks.note: first meaning: courage, strength of character
second meaning: the Scots form of great, as in great with young, pregnant

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like butchery, a spine in a lamb joint; 'in lamb' describes a pregnant ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbone means resolve and determination; in Scots, a ewe carrying a lamb is great, written as this word.

clue.text: Glum line adopted by Smithers surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order
adopted by means taken in by, so the piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mr Smithers unexpectedly takes on a gloomy expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirthless means without joy or laughter, so a glum, cheerless person or smile is described this way.

clue.text: For instance, cracking opinions may be frightful things

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: my bet is that... means my opinion is
as in examples such as these means for instance

explanation.surface: Some brilliant opinions turn out to be scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like praise for the opinions; it signals one piece breaking into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts can mean brutal or horrible creatures, or unpleasant things in general, so these are fearsome objects.

clue.text: Supplier ripped into Sister

indicators.note: into means placed inside another piece

blocks.note: SR is the abbreviation for sister
tore is the past tense of tear, ripped

explanation.surface: A vendor laid into a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A storer keeps stock and provides goods from it, so acts as a provider of supplies.
